cleo_hotel.png.note: Real plan. Captions are English plus one misspelled French word (RÉGÉPTION), and a demo heatmap is baked into the image. 'restroom' is the check that needs vision rather than caption transcription: the bathrooms are drawn as unlabelled fixtures. NOT a hold-out — this is also the E2E fixture, so it is the most overfit input in the repo.

cafe_vector.pdf.note: Synthetic but measured: double-line walls, door swing arcs, furniture, scale bar, 1:100 title block. Generated from an explicit room model, so every caption is provably inside its own room.

coworking_vector.pdf.note: Second venue type. The exterior door is drawn on the reception's south wall, so expect_entrance is evidenced by the drawing rather than inferred.

sales_chart.png.note: Bar chart. Intake must reject it AND say why in a sentence — accepting this is the product's worst failure mode, so both of its checks are hard.

blackstone_hotel_1910.png.note: A REAL HOLD-OUT: the Blackstone Hotel, Chicago (Marshall & Fox, c.1910), public domain via Wikimedia Commons. Nothing about this product influenced it — unlike cleo_hotel.png, which is also the E2E fixture. Four floor plates on one sheet, which is normal architectural practice and which used to blow the Zone Analyst's token budget outright; the prompt now scopes to the ground/entrance plate. Period labels (Lounging Room, Buffet, Ball Room, Cigar Stand) test function-not-wording classification on vocabulary no modern plan uses. Its retail concessions (Flower Shop, Shop, Barber Shop) are why ZoneCategory gained a `retail` value on 2026-08-08 — they had been landing in `other`, taking a default attraction in the flow simulation and a default floor share in the solver. This plan now REQUIRES retail, which is the check that would catch the category being dropped or the analyst forgetting it exists. A small allowance remains for the double-height voids ("Upper Part of…"), which genuinely are not floor zones.
